results.summary_before: This project implements AND, NAND, and NOT gates, as well as an SR latch built from two NOR gates with feedback. The documentation provides detailed instructions for testing, including power setup, verifying basic gates, and testing the latch behavior. External hardware includes momentary pushbuttons, pull-up resistors, LEDs or a 7-segment display, and a breadboard with a regulated supply.

results.summary_before: This combinational design feeds four pairs of inputs through XOR gates, combines those results with two AND gates, and passes the final result through an XNOR gate to all eight outputs. The intended test is to set all inputs low, or to set one input of each pair high and the other low, and confirm the outputs are asserted in both cases. No external hardware is needed. The documentation is clear about the gate topology but does not explain a practical application.

results.summary_before: This project implements a tapped delay line using a chain of inverters and flip-flops, with eight tap outputs and a multiplexer to select which tap to observe. It is designed to measure the propagation delay between start and stop signals, serving as a characterization test for future projects. External hardware such as a signal generator and possibly an FPGA is suggested for testing. The design's main purpose is to evaluate timing characteristics, and no silicon results are provided.

results.summary_before: This design is a 4-bit Johnson counter that generates four offset square waves at one-quarter of the input clock frequency. It is built from four D flip-flops connected in a ring with the inverted output of the last stage fed back to the first. The outputs can be verified with a logic analyzer to observe the expected repeating pattern. No external hardware is required, and the design is a straightforward sequential logic example.

results.summary_before: This project counts from 0 to 7 and displays the digit on a 7-segment LCD, incrementing every second. It converts a 3-bit binary-coded decimal to the seven segment outputs using truth tables, sum-of-products, Boolean simplification, and Karnaugh mapping. The design is controlled by a clock switch and a reset button to start from zero. No external hardware is needed, and it appears to be an educational exercise in combinational logic design.
